Sam (Support): Customer #5820 sees client drop mid-stream when switching networks (WiFi -> cellular). They get partial chunks, then stream closes after ~6s. App v3.4.1 iOS 16.4. Repro: start streaming generation in app, enable background audio, toggle WiFi off. Attaching logs below. Can we triage?

Ashley (Mobile Eng): Thanks — is this SSE or WebSocket from the app? Any auth/token refresh happening at the same time? Do we have the exact request? @Leo any proxy logs? :eyes:

Sam (Support): SSE from the app. No explicit token refresh during test. Sample request (redacted API key) below: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","stream":true,"max_tokens":1024}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
```

Leo (Infra): I pulled the edge logs for that customer span. Around the time of the reported drop we see repeated: 
```
2026-04-11T17:02:13Z proxy[envoy]: client closed connection (ECONNRESET) from 10.2.1.5:53724
2026-04-11T17:02:19Z upstream[svc-infer]: upstream EOF while streaming
```
This lines up with the 6s gap you mentioned. Envoy marks the socket closed because the client TCP FIN/RST arrived after interface change. Kernel-level behavior on iOS can cancel outstanding tasks quickly when the network stack flips.

Ashley (Mobile Eng): On the device logs I see NSURLSessionTask taskIdentifier=42 finished with error -999 and NSURLErrorNetworkConnectionLost. No token refresh attempt logged. The client tries to re-open the SSE but receives 401 on the very first reconnect attempt — token lifetime is fine but refresh flow races with reconnect when app is backgrounded.

Sam (Support): Customer is worried about partial responses and billing — they say the stream produced two partial paragraphs and then stopped, but they were charged for the request. Any guidance?

Priya (Billing): We bill for tokens produced (server-side). If the model generated tokens before the stream closed, those tokens count. If it's clearly a service-side fault we can evaluate credits, but client-triggered disconnects (network flip) generally aren't eligible. We can offer a one-off credit while infra investigates.

Leo (Infra): Short-term mitigations:
- Increase TCP keepalive intervals on edge (risk: small extra load)
- Tune Envoy idle/stream timeouts to be slightly more permissive for mobile flows
- Add a small buffer window server-side to wait for rapid reconnects (detect same client/session and allow resume within N seconds) — requires protocol work (resume token) and product discussion.

Ashley (Mobile Eng): On our side we can:
- Add a reconnect/backoff that retries automatically without forcing token refresh immediately (so reconnects within a short window reuse valid auth)
- Surface a better UX on lock/unlock network swaps
We can prototype a quick client change to hold the connection alive for ~10s after a network change and to retry transparently.

Sam (Support): Plan: gather full pcap and device console logs from customer, try repro with WiFi toggle on local test device, and coordinate a quick infra tuning (keepalive + timeout bump) as an interim. Scheduling triage call 16:00 PT today. I'll attach logs to the ticket and request credit approval flow if needed. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0458 - streaming client disconnects on network swap. Assigned to: Leo, Ashley.

Ashley (Mobile Eng): Sounds good — Sam, please also capture the exact SSE headers and any proxy IPs so we can correlate.

Sam (Support): Will do. I'll upload pcap + console logs to the ticket and ping here once done. Thanks everyone. :pray:
